To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a body fixed coordinate system for the inertial measurements results in a higher accuracy than using a sensor fixed coordinate system.
the approach using an IMU as reference frame outperforms the approach using a camera frame as reference frame.

the use of an IMU in combination with a camera is a promising approach for the localization of pedestrians in indoor environments, that the approach with a fixed IMU frame of reference is more robust against noise, and that the approach with the IMU frame of references fixed to the camera is less susceptible to drift.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can inertial information be integrated into a monocular EKF-based SLAM system in a way that the resulting filter can be used to estimate the position and orientation of a sensor attached to the pedestrian?
the following questions: How can the visual and inertial measurements be combined in order to achieve an accurate localization of a pedestrian?
the following questions: (i) How can a monocular SLAM system be improved by using an inertial measurement system?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both approaches perform equally well.
both methods are applicable for a monocular SLAM system, however, they differ in terms of the reference frame and the way how the IMU measurements are handled.
the two different approaches are equally suitable for an inertial aided monovision SLAM system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the approach which uses an inertial reference frame is superior to the one which uses a camera reference frame.
both approaches are capable of providing a good localization performance in the presence of drift.
the use of a fixed body frame for the inertial integration is superior to a fixed world frame in terms of the accuracy of the localization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the reference system has an impact on the accuracy of the SLAM algorithm.
the choice of reference system has an important impact on the accuracy and robustness of an EKF-SLAMS system.
the choice of reference system is a crucial aspect of the integration of visual and inertial sensor measurements.
